title: Component Garden: Figma library for telemetry-aware cost & rollout primitives
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a coherent, telemetry-aware Figma component library (the 'Component Garden') that consolidates rollout controls, cost-insight primitives, and compact dashboard elements. This ticket scopes the prototype, accessibility pass, handoff tokens, and a lightweight audit checklist for consumption by ENG and PM. Goal: reduce implementation divergence across Console cost views and rollout surfaces and provide a ready-to-use Figma kit plus documentation for rollout state transitions and cost signal visualizations.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library published with a master page containing: rollout strip, canary badge, cost microcard, tokenized metric chip, and compact timeline component
Token mapping document (color/spacing/typography) linked from the Figma file and synced with the token token-bridge repo
Accessibility checks: contrast, keyboard focus, and screen reader labels documented for each component
Design review approved by PM and Eng (sign-offs present in comments) and a handoff checklist shared
Two reference screens (Cost Overview and Rollouts Dashboard) implemented in prototype showing token usage and telemetry overlays
comments: 2025-02-10 Asha: Created initial brief and scoped components. Primary focus on cost microcard, rollout strip, metric chip, and compact timeline. Tagged ENG and PM for dependency alignment.
2025-02-12 Luis: Uploaded first Figma frames; requested guidance on token naming (asked whether we should mirror runtime token names or create UI-facing aliases).
2025-02-13 PM (Marianne Ku): Asked to prioritize canary/rollback affordances for safety-critical rollouts. Suggested adding a passive telemetry overlay to show recent error rate and cost delta.

2025-02-14 Design review: noted that compact timeline vertical rhythm conflicts with existing metric chip spacing; proposed introducing a 'micro-gap' spacing token. Action: add token variant and update token mapping doc.

2025-02-16 ENG (Rao): Flagged implementation risk for live telemetry overlays on low-tier Dedicated customers due to sampling constraints. Trade-off: provide static snapshot variant with hover-to-refresh as fallback.
2025-02-18 Accessibility review (Iris): Contrast on the canary badge fails WCAG AA at small sizes. Action: adjust hue ramp and add a thicker outline token for critical badges.
2025-02-19 Luis: Pushed token bridge PR linking figma variables to token repo and added mapping table in Confluence. PR #128 created.
2025-02-20 PM (Marianne): Design reviewed and approved pending two small follow-ups (contrast tweak and fallback behavior doc). Marking this ticket In Review.
2025-02-20 Asha: Uploaded final prototype and handoff checklist. Next step: coordinate with ENG for a pilot implementation in the cost-explorer route.
decisions: Use UI-facing alias tokens separate from runtime tokens to allow visual tuning without changing backend semantics
Provide two rendering modes for telemetry overlays: live sampled overlay and static snapshot fallback for low-capacity deployments
Adopt an explicit micro-spacing token ('spacing.mg') for compact components to preserve vertical rhythm across cards and rails
tradeoffs: Live telemetry overlays improve signal but add sampling/latency complexity; chosen fallback keeps rollout UX consistent while deferring sampling work to a follow-up ENG ticket
Introducing UI aliases increases mapping maintenance but enables quicker visual iterations without risking runtime compatibility
next_steps: ENG: Coordinate pilot on cost-explorer route (ENG owner: Rao) - create ENG ticket for implementation and sampling strategy
Design: Perform accessibility pass on canary and badge tokens and publish updated tokens to the Confluence mapping
PM: Schedule rollout with QA for pilot cohort and prepare release notes documenting fallback modes
Follow-up ticket: DES-999999 (create a usability study for microcard comprehension during rollouts)
review_notes: Key feedback: clarity of state transitions in rollout strip, visible cost deltas without clutter, and keyboard navigability of microcards
Approval: PM and Eng gave conditional sign-off on 2025-02-20; accessibility fixes required before final close
ux_considerations: Prefer compact affordances with discoverable expanded details (hover/keyboard trigger)
Avoid using color as the sole indicator for rollout states; pair with iconography and text labels
Ensure metric chips remain readable at 12px with line-height token and increased numeric weight
